item.title: Tom Brady seemingly fires shot at ex-wife Gisele Bundchen with Jordan Love and Christian Watson take
item.description: Photo by Theo Wargo/WireImage Tom Brady was on the call during the New England Patriots’ loss to the Green Bay Packers and seemingly poked fun at his divorce from supermodel Gisele Bundchen. Bundchen and Brady were married from 2009 to 2022, with their divorce coming about because of Brady’s unwillingness to retire without returning to the NFL. After the celebrity power couple split, Brady embarked on his post-NFL career with the Las Vegas Raiders and as a commentator for Fox Sports. Did Tom Brady take a dig at ex-wife Gisele Bundchen during Patriots vs. Packers comments? During the Green Bay Packers’ win against the New England Patriots, Tom Brady was amazed by the chemistry between QB Jordan Love and WR Christian Watson. He likened their trust in each other to the type of trust that makes a marriage successful, which many have perceived as a dig at his ex-wife, Gisele Bundchen. Brady remarked: “Oh my gosh. That trust between Jordan Love and Watson – only a marriage could dream of that type of trust.” While the comment might seem innocuous to some, there is a good reason why fans are suggesting that Brady took a dig at his ex-wife. During their divorce proceedings, the rumour, innuendo, and conjecture alleged that Bundchen had engaged in an extramarital affair prior to the couple’s separation. While the Brazilian supermodel has denied these allegations vociferously, it hasn’t stopped the world from running with this narrative. Jokes about this alleged affair from Bundchen have become a common talking point when it comes to Tom Brady, with his publicised 2023 Roast featuring many jokes and references to it. However, the trust comment could also be Brady poking fun at his own shortcomings in his marriage to Bundchen. According to sources, one of the reasons the marriage between the two collapsed was because of Brady allegedly walking back on his promise to retire from the NFL for one more season. Regardless of Brady’s intent, his offhand remark has become one of the biggest talking points of the weekend, even beyond some of the big results in the NFL. (Photo by Ed Zurga/Getty Images) | Getty Images UCF and chaotic, seemingly inexplicable finishes have become quite the pairing this season. Two weeks after knocking off BYU in perhaps the wildest ending of the college football season , the Knights found themselves in another crunch time thriller Saturday, this time on the road at Kansas. For most of the contest, UCF appeared on track to secure its first comfortable victory in Big 12 play. The Knights built a 26-7 lead by the 9:52 mark of the third quarter, seemingly having solved the Jayhawks on both sides of the ball. But their next two possessions went nowhere, producing consecutive three-and-outs that combined for -6 yards. That sudden offensive futility left the door ajar for a Kansas comeback, and the Jayhawks capitalized with two-straight touchdown drives and a field goal to trim the deficit to 26-24. Then, following a spectacular punt by Atticus Bertrams, Kansas regained possession at its own 5-yard line with 2:27 remaining, needing just a field goal to complete the program’s largest comeback since 2010. Somehow, the Jayhawks crammed 11 plays and 95 yards into 81 seconds, capping the clutch drive with a Dylan Edwards touchdown run with 1:06 remaining, catapulting Kansas ahead 32-26. But the scoring drive was so quick that it granted UCF 66 seconds of opportunity while armed with two timeouts. The drive did not start in promising fashion as the Knights opened the drive with several misfires. But quarterback Alonza Barnett III — making his first start since suffering a hamstring injury in Week 2 — caught fire, jumpstarting the offense with a 20-yard completion to Tyren Hornes on 3rd-and-10. item.title: On the future of the NBA in Mexico, from the Global Games to a franchise
item.description: MEXICO CITY: No city outside the United States or Canada has hosted more regular season NBA games than Mexico City. So it should come as no surprise that the annual tilts held in the Mexican capital are the frequent backdrop for rumbles about the league setting up shop on a more permanent basis in the largest metropolis on the continent. In recent years, however, the league making a return to the Pacific Northwest to put a new team back in Seattle, Washington along with a new team in Las Vegas, Nevada seemed a fait accompli, and with it, hope for an NBA team in the city faded. But before the start of the 2026 season, it was announced at an NBA Board of Governor's meeting that Mexico City was back in the mix with a potential ownership group and arena district lined up. Still, the Mexico City Game has been and will likely remain the gem in the crown of the league that is their Global Games series, a yearly accomplishment on its own signifying the nascent talent and fandom of Latin America now percolating into the league's ranks. To learn more, the Rookie Wire caught up with NBA Latin America and Canada Head of Operations Raul Zarraga ahead of the 2026 Mexico City Game between the Denver Nuggets and Indiana Pacers . From the state of the Association in Mexico, and what the future of Mexico City Games and NBA expansion in the region might look like, our conversation covered the gamut and then some. This interview has been lightly edited for the purposes of clarity and brevity. Rookie Wire: What it is you do with regard to the Mexico City games? Raul Zarraga : Of course. The Global Game – it's a great opportunity for us. You have this life experience for fans and partners and everyone in the community, and all the people enjoying the game. Keep in mind that less than one percent of people around the world have the opportunity to be in-person for a regular season NBA game. And that's why it's very important for us to give a piece of that action to all the fans in Mexico. I wish we could have many more games available for fans. But we are very happy with the experience so far. It's sold out in a couple of days. The two amazing teams, we're really looking forward to (having them) here: the Pacers and the Nuggets. The Pacers for the first time, the Nuggets the second, and it's a whole celebration together, a unique way to mix two very important components: entertainment and the culture. Something that the fans are really looking for, regardless if they are core, casual, (or) curious fans of our 30 million fans (in Latin America), this is a great opportunity to enjoy the NBA. So we have this regular season (game), and then we tip off the season for Capitanes for 21 games of regular season happening here. item.title: Best division ever? How NFC North is on pace to make history in 2026
item.description: Best division ever? How NFC North is on pace to make history in 2026 originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Bears found a way to win on Sunday night, overcoming five turnovers to defeat the Buccaneers 27-24, but they certainly aren't alone in the NFC North. The Packers and Lions both continued their winning ways on Sunday, and, until Monday at least, none of those three teams can say they only one loss like the Vikings do. All four NFC North teams will enter Week 10 in the playoff picture. While head-to-head matchups might hurt the division's chances of getting every team into the playoffs, it's becoming clear these four teams are in a class of their own as a group. Here's a look at how the NFC North could be headed for uncharted territory. MORE: Which NFL trade candidates boosted - or hurt - their stocks in Week 9? NFC North combined record The NFC North is now 25-8 (.757) through nearly nine weeks, with five of those eight losses simply coming against one another. NFC North teams are 20-3 in non-divisional games. Here are the standings after Sunday night, with the Vikings still to play on Monday: Team Record Pct. Vikings 6-1 .857 Bears 7-2 .778 Lions 6-2 .750 Packers 6-3 .667 Every team in the division is at least three games over .500, meaning the Packers are in last place at 6-3. In the NFC North, for comparison, the 3-5 Panthers lead the division. The Bears have had a hard time gaining ground during the four-game win streak because of all of the success around them, but a Vikings loss to the Bills on Monday night would rocket Chicago into first place. MORE: 4 quarterbacks who boosted their early MVP cases in Week 9 Best division in NFL history When it comes to divisions, there are two distinct periods in the NFL: pre-2002, when divisions were larger than four teams, and 2002-present, when all divisions have been comprised of four teams. The overall records within divisions were more even before 2002 because more teams were in each. Since 2002, the best record for a division belongs to the 2024 NFC North, which saw teams go a combined 45-23 (.662) as the Lions went 15-2, Vikings went 14-3, Packers went 11-6 and Bears went 7-10. Two years earlier, in the NFC East went a combined 43-23-2, sending three teams to the playoffs. So far, the NFC North is on track to break its own record in 2026. At 25-8 (.757), every team is at least three games above .500 and their combined record would have to be 20-15 the rest of the way to match the 2024 mark. There are still seven divisional games on the docket in the NFC North, so the division will have at least 15 losses. If these four teams can keep it to only eight additional losses, the division will tie its own record from 2002. item.title: Mitch Albom: Lions won't have many easy wins. But does it matter?
item.description: Dan Campbell knew what this was by halftime. He barked it into the CBS cameras. “We gotta calm down … and then we GOTTA GO! We can’t be messing around!” Exactly. When playing a team that is 1-6, a good team often finds itself inexplicably fumbling and bumbling. It’s like when you can’t get that first piece of plastic to peel off the box. You start normal, then you try your fingernails, then you get frustrated, and you wind up screaming to yourself, “Why is this so damn hard?” That was the Detroit Lions for much of Sunday’s game in Miami against the low-win but high-effort Dolphins . Detroit’s first drive used up nearly seven minutes but ended with a sack of Jared Goff on third-and-goal. A field goal had to suffice. Their second drive ended in an interception, when Goff was pressured and a defender hit his arm as he tried to pass. Their third drive ended with a punt. Their fourth drive, after starting with great field position, fizzled when Jahmyr Gibbs was yanked down twice in a row for thre- yard losses and Goff was pressured into a scramble. Another field goal. The NFL’s highest-flying offense was hovering very close to the ground. Fortunately, Miami couldn’t take advantage. They punted twice, notched a field goal, and wasted an 11-play drive with a doink off the uprights by their kicker, Zane Gonzalez. Halftime ended at Lions 6, Miami 3. Which is what led Campbell to his “we can’t be messing around” critique, which I’m sure he delivered in the locker room with a fervor that would have scared the average TV viewer. And eventually, they did stop messing around. And they finally brought home a 19-9 win that may have certain critics attacking them for, well, not being able to get the plastic off a box faster than that. They’d be wrong. It swirled around practice all week. When one football player sees another football player face down and not moving, it stays with them − believe me. Although Gaethje initially ruled out an immediate rematch, his stance has seemingly softened since then. However, the lightweight champion is yet to make a decision about his future and remains uncertain about whether he wants to compete again. Meanwhile, Topuria has hinted at an April 2027 return in his first interview since the White House event. He also recently asked his Instagram followers whether they would rather see him run it back with Gaethje or settle his long-running rivalry with Paddy Pimblett. The results heavily favored a rematch with Gaethje. However, Ali Abdelaziz believes fans shouldn’t get their hopes up , as he doesn’t see that fight happening. Ali Abdelaziz Admits Ilia Topuria’s Recent Career Revelation Was True Topuria recently took to Instagram to ask his followers which opponent they wanted to see him face next. item.description: Effort is difficult to quantify in the NBA. However, there are a few areas of the game that can occasionally reveal its presence. For an example of this phenomenon during the Boston Celtics' 117-97 win over the Milwaukee Bucks on Sunday night, look no further than the final offensive rebound totals. The C's corralled a whopping 20 offensive boards at Fiserv Forum in Milwaukee while the Bucks only grabbed 9. Such a significant disparity suggests that the Celtics, who trailed 20-6 about halfway through the first quarter, stepped up their effort when things didn't immediately go their way. In fact, 4 of Boston's 6 offensive rebounds in the first frame occurred after it went down double digits. Meanwhile, Milwaukee had 0 offensive rebounds in that same span, and just 1 in the entire first quarter. Because the Celtics dominated the glass, they ended up with 16 more field goal attempts than the Bucks. From there, it's a math game, as Boston converted on 45 of its 95 shots (47.4 percent from the field) while Milwaukee hit 35 of its 79 shots (44.3 percent from the field). As for the rest of the margins, the Celtics garnered 12 steals — another effort-related stat — to the Bucks' 5 and prevailed in the points in the paint battle, 44-28. All of these numbers added up to the Celtics' third straight win and the Bucks' sixth straight loss. item.description: Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images Jordan Love has backed Matt LaFleur’s decision to keep attacking despite the Green Bay Packers holding a 20-point lead against the New England Patriots. The Packers were leading 34-14 late in the third quarter when they recovered a Patriots fumble. Rather than slow things down, LaFleur called for a deep pass that ended with Christian Watson scoring a 39-yard touchdown. Green Bay eventually secured a 45-27 victory, with Love throwing for 372 yards and three touchdowns as the Packers improved to 6-3. Jordan Love praises Matt LaFleur’s aggressive approach against New England Patriots Love was pleased that LaFleur refused to take his foot off the gas, particularly with the Patriots still capable of making a comeback. Speaking after the game, the quarterback said: “I love being aggressive. I love the way Matt [LaFleur] called the game tonight,” The touchdown pass to Watson stretched Green Bay’s advantage to 40-14. Love then added a successful two-point conversion himself, taking the lead to 28 points. LaFleur shared his quarterback’s approach, explaining that he did not believe the Packers could afford to relax against a talented opponent. He was also reluctant to take his starters out too early after recalling a previous game in Dallas that made him wary of allowing an opponent back into contention. Watson was one of the biggest beneficiaries of Green Bay’s attacking approach. He finished with seven receptions for a career-high 171 yards and a touchdown, while Matthew Golden recorded 10 catches for 164 yards and another score. item.title: LeBron James shines as Sixers down Bulls
item.description: Veteran superstar LeBron James scored 22 points with five assists, returning to form (Michael Reaves) LeBron James had his best game yet for the Philadelphia 76ers, who bounced back with a 127-121 win in Chicago on Sunday over a Bulls side that has now lost seven straight NBA games. Veteran superstar James scored 22 points -- his highest tally since joining the Sixers this summer -- in a return to form after a paltry eight points in Friday's disappointing loss to Cleveland. James also had five assists while Jaylen Brown top-scored with 29, Tyrese Maxey poured in 27 and Joel Embiid pulled down 10 rebounds. The star-studded Sixers have lost just twice so far this season, for their best start after 11 games since 2000. Philadelphia grabbed the lead early in the second quarter and never trailed from there, though a resilient Chicago pulled within two points in the closing stages. "We have a lot of guys that's been in situations, late-game situations, and we have a 'no panic' button," said James. "We understand that we got to get stops on this end, but if teams make a run, we understand how to be calm on the other end as well." The Bulls remain second-bottom of the Eastern Conference, ahead of only the Milwaukee Bucks -- the only team Chicago has beaten so far this campaign. They were without shooting guard Norman Powell, their second-leading scorer this season, who was placed on the injury report hours before tip-off with back discomfort. But Josh Giddey provided some hope with a double-double including 19 points and 15 assists. Meanwhile, James' former Los Angeles Lakers team overcame the absence of red-hot talisman Luka Doncic to beat the Detroit Pistons 121-116, and also move to 9-2. Doncic, who has been averaging more than 40 points per game this season, was left out with lower back tightness, the team announced. Austin Reaves stepped up, scoring 43 points, including two calm free throws in the final seconds to take the game beyond Detroit's reach. The Lakers never trailed but had to fight hard to retain a razor-thin lead for most of the fourth quarter. Daniss Jenkins led the Pistons' comeback attempt from the bench with 31 points, while Kevin Huerter added 24. Minnesota extended its fine start with a 115-100 win over struggling Utah. It was the Timberwolves' fourth straight win despite losing Anthony Edwards to injury. The Bucks suffered another loss, falling 117-97 to the Celtics, who rallied from an early 14-point deficit, while Dallas thumped Brooklyn 130-93. Giannis Antetokounmpo top-scored for Miami in a 114-108 win at Sacramento with 29 points and 14 rebounds, while the Los Angeles Clippers grabbed a rare win, defeating New Orleans 139-123. The Charlotte Hornets announced that forward Kon Knueppel will miss at least four weeks with a left hamstring strain, while guard Dennis Schroder is out for at least two weeks with the same injury. amz/js
